title: Insiders updates
summary: New features, improvements, and fixes in Tempo Insiders builds.
body_markdown:
Tempo Insiders builds ship ahead of the stable channel, so these notes are incremental: each entry covers only what landed since the previous Insiders build. Every stable release bundles the builds that preceded it — see[Product updates](https://docs.tempo.new/changelog) for the merged notes.

**Visual Review launches with onboarding, a published CLI, and PR diff review.**


### ​


New


- Visual Review: onboarding flow with doctor, init, and setup status checks.
- Visual Review CLI (@tempo-ai/visual-review) is now published.
- Visual Review can link PRs and surface visual diffs for review.
- Google Fonts in the style panel font picker, with an AI-mode install handoff.
- Canvas supports dropping multiple HTML files at once.
- Secondary chat tabs can now live inside a root chat’s tab set.
- Codex adds the GPT-6 Astra model with a max effort setting.


### ​


Improved


- Projection surface renders live canvas pixels on demand.
- Cached storyboard captures show while the devserver is still booting.


### ​


Fixed


- Space+drag on a storyboard header now pans instead of moving the board.
- Codex no longer double-renders your images when a thread reloads.
- Canvas setup now works for empty projects.
- Two canvases on one host no longer deadlock projection startup.
- Canvas host install failures now keep the real error on screen.
- The app-exit notice in chat can now be dismissed.


This release centers on **Visual Review** . A new onboarding flow (doctor, init, and setup status checks) gets you started, the` @tempo-ai/visual-review` CLI is now published, and you can link PRs and review visual diffs directly — including clearer diff highlighting and changed-card previews. A getting-started guide is available to walk through the workflow.


**Canvas** gets several upgrades: the projection surface now renders live canvas pixels on demand, cached storyboard captures paint while the devserver boots, and you can drop multiple HTML files at once. A batch of fixes make canvas more reliable — Space+drag on storyboard headers pans correctly, empty projects set up properly, two canvases on one host no longer deadlock, and host install failures surface the real cause.


On the **Chat and Agents** side, you can now open secondary chat tabs inside a root chat’s tab set, Codex adds the GPT-6 Astra model with a max effort option, and system prompts are frozen per provider session so preserved thinking stays intact. The style panel also gains Google Fonts with an AI-assisted install handoff.

On the **AI chat** side, in-chat` Cmd+F` now highlights, counts, and navigates matches in a single display index, and we restored the todo panel and CLI trust prompt. We also added **Claude Fable 5.1** to the model picker and retired Fable 5.

On the reliability side, verdicts you submit now survive the sign-in window instead of being dropped, and the canvas root context menu opens correctly on storyboard headers and empty frames.

This release is heavy on stability. A renderer crash no longer brings down the entire app, dead renderers now reload themselves, and previously silent main-process failures are surfaced instead of masked. Hidden surfaces also stop subscribing in the background, so agent runs report their status honestly.


Canvas gets meaningful additions: you can preview and edit structural gestures right inside AI mode, Chromium installs automatically on your first canvas capture, and AI-mode chrome now looks right in light mode while respecting your saved backdrops. Several canvas rough edges are gone too — the interact spinner no longer hangs, slug-linked canvases open and preview correctly, and search returns canvases from the workspace you’re currently in.


Chat adds a select mode with multi-select checkboxes and a bulk-action bar, and chats now reopen where you left off. Agents get a single list-settings control with a saveable default. On the platform side, updates wait for in-flight installs to finish, remote control recovers cleanly from identity resets, invite-by-email is tidier, and AI usage billing scans stay within their intended windows.

The cloud-ready` @tempo-ai/mcp` package adds personal access tokens and a universal CLI, so canvas sharing now works from any cloud agent, not just local setups. We also tightened up a few rough edges—bug report bundles are now capped to stay under the 200 MB upload limit, visual review approvals are gated by your organization membership, and the stray dev-server warning toast is gone.

Canvas is the center of this release. You can now author across frameworks — Svelte components, AI-generated React snapshots, and static HTML route snapshots — plus drag in raw HTML files and create components straight from a selection. Frame-size presets, folder cards that open the all-canvases modal, and a batch of selection, grouping, and layout fixes make everyday editing steadier.


AI and chat get more control and reliability. You can set per-device API keys for AI providers under Settings → Preferences → Providers, fork a chat from any message, and @-mention an agent to run a task without attaching a ticket. Several long-standing annoyances are gone: Codex no longer prompts for your Keychain password on every spawn, sends won’t silently downgrade to an unfundable BYOK route, and Windows Git credential prompts have stopped recurring.


The new external` @tempo/mcp` server lets you expose Tempo’s toolsets to other MCP clients, with an install guide included. Issues, Workspaces, and pricing round things out — Stages editing moved into Organization settings, archived workspaces sort by activity, focus is preserved when switching workspaces, and a new pricing page introduces a $200 Team plan for 5 seats.

The canvas gets a batch of meaningful upgrades. You can paste HTML and URLs directly as live storyboards, live shape previews render smoothly while drawing, interact-mode zoom tracks the canvas, and color-picker edits now collapse into a single undo step with undo stacks scoped per workspace.


Chat and agents are steadier too. Interrupted turns are resumable, expanded diffs no longer bleed between chats, history replay won’t destructively shrink, and background agent runs stop hijacking your active workspace. The Agents tab also moves to a sidebar-driven layout.


Across the platform we fixed sharing and invitation flows, cleared the lingering post-wake auth toast, stopped docs and issues from dropping images, and resolved a macOS release crash — plus faster, lower-churn workspace switching.
